content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Pittsburgh

steps_items.heading: 1. Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a combination of formal education and project-management experience. Review PMI's specific prerequisites for the PMP credential—typically a bachelor's degree plus documented hours leading projects, or equivalent alternative pathways. Granite PM Academy's advisors can help you verify your qualifications before enrollment.

steps_items.heading: 2. Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP course. All sessions are online and scheduled to fit working professionals' calendars. You'll engage with active certified practitioners covering the PMBOK® Guide framework, real-world case studies, and exam-focused content—all required to sit for the certification exam.

steps_items.heading: 3. Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After finishing coursework, apply directly to PMI with proof of your education and project experience. Pay the associated exam fee through PMI's official portal. Granite PM Academy staff can guide you through the application process and answer questions about documentation and deadlines.

steps_items.heading: 4. Prepare and Pass the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice tests, study guides, and Q&A support—to reinforce your knowledge. Schedule your proctored exam through PMI's testing partner. On exam day, you'll demonstrate mastery of project-management principles and advance your career in Pittsburgh's growing professional sectors.

steps_items.heading: 5. Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: The PMP credential renews every three years. Earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) through project work, training, volunteer activities, or continuing education. Granite PM Academy offers ongoing learning resources to help you meet PMI's renewal requirements and stay current in the discipline.

fq_items.question: Do I need to travel to {city} for this training?
fq_items.answer: No. All of our PMP training is delivered live-virtual via video conference, so {city} professionals attend from wherever they work. No commuting or hotel required.

fq_items.question: What are the PMP eligibility requirements?
fq_items.answer: PMI sets four eligibility paths based on education: a secondary diploma (high school or equivalent) requires 60 months of project leadership experience; an associate's degree requires 48 months; a bachelor's degree requires 36 months; and a bachelor's or postgraduate degree from a PMI Global Accreditation Center (GAC)-accredited program requires just 24 months. Every path also requires 35 hours of project management education — our course satisfies this requirement in full.

fq_items.question: How long does it take to get PMP certified in {city}?
fq_items.answer: After completing training, PMI typically approves applications within 5–10 business days. Once approved, you have one year to sit for the exam. Most students study 4–8 weeks after the course before scheduling their exam.

fq_items.question: What is your pass guarantee?
fq_items.answer: If you complete our course and do not pass the PMP exam within 90 days, we provide additional coaching sessions at no additional cost until you pass.

fq_items.question: Is this training PMI-approved?
fq_items.answer: Yes. Granite PM Academy is a PMI Premier Authorized Training Partner (ATP). Our curriculum is aligned to PMI’s current Examination Content Outline and our contact hours are fully accepted by PMI.

fq_items.answer: Pittsburgh's largest employers—PNC Financial Services, PPG Industries, UPMC, Highmark Health, Wabtec, and University of Pittsburgh—routinely manage complex capital projects requiring coordinated teams and formal governance. The PMP credential signals mastery of those frameworks. While no Pittsburgh-specific salary premium has been independently verified, PMI's national research shows certified project managers earn a median of $135,000 versus $109,157 for non-certified peers. That differential holds across most regions, making certification a reasonable differentiator for advancement in Pittsburgh's financial-services, healthcare, and advanced-manufacturing sectors.

fq_items.answer: Financial services, healthcare systems, materials and chemicals manufacturing, rail and transportation equipment, and higher education dominate Pittsburgh's economy. All five sectors coordinate multi-year, multi-stakeholder projects—think healthcare facility expansions, capital equipment deployments, or infrastructure modernization. Employers in these industries routinely list PMP certification as preferred or required for senior project and program management roles, particularly as projects grow in scope and cross-functional complexity.

This format suits Pittsburgh professionals managing demanding schedules at PNC, UPMC, Highmark, PPG, Wabtec, and Pitt.
